'''Yaroslav Mikhaylovich Blanter''' ({{langx|ru|Ярослав Михайлович Блантер}}; born 19 November 1967) is a Russian [[physicist]], an expert in the field of [[extractive metallurgy]] and [[condensed matter physics]]. {{As of|2011|post=,}} he is a professor at the [[Delft University of Technology]].<ref name="esq"/><ref name=CV /><ref>{{cite web|url=http://expertcorps.ru/science/experts/branch/cond-mat/all|title=Condensed Matter Physics: All Experts|website=Corpus expertov|archive-date=14 July 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190714222601/expertcorps.ru/science/experts/branch/cond-mat/all|access-date=17 July 2018|language=ru-RU|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://casimir.researchschool.nl/yaroslav-blanter-appointed-to-antoni-van-leeuwenhoek-chair-1700.html|title=Casimir - Yaroslav Blanter appointed to Antoni van Leeuwenhoek chair|website=Casimir Research School|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190510212538/casimir.researchschool.nl/yaroslav-blanter-appointed-to-antoni-van-leeuwenhoek-chair.html|archive-date=10 May 2019|access-date=17 July 2018|url-status=live}}</ref>

==Biography==
Blanter was born in [[Moscow]], Russia. In 1984, he graduated from the Second physico-mathematical school of Moscow.<ref>[https://web.archive.org/web/20040825174609/http://www.school2.ru/who-is-who/cgi-bin/who-is-who.pl?year=1984 List of 2nd schools alumni of 1984]. Second physico-mathematical school of Moscow. Archived from [http://www.school2.ru/who-is-who/cgi-bin/who-is-who.pl?year=1984 the original] on 25 August 2004.</ref>

In 1990, he graduated from the physicochemical department of the [[Moscow Institute of Steel and Alloys]] in the field of [[extractive metallurgy]].<ref>[http://misis.ru/Portals/0/Vipusknikam/vipuskniki_1985-1994.pdf Moscow Institute of Steel and Alloys alumni of 1985-1994]. Moscow, publ. «Учеба» МИСиС (in Russian). 2006. {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090306093750/http://misis.ru/Portals/0/Vipusknikam/vipuskniki_1985-1994.pdf |date=6 March 2009 }} </ref>

Until 1992, he took post-graduate courses at the same institute. In 1992, he defended his thesis and received the [[Candidate of Sciences|Candidate of physico-mathematical sciences]] degree. The subject of the thesis concerned the development of the quantum effects in the kinetic properties of the electronic systems at the topological transition.<ref>[http://old.rsl.ru/table.jsp?f=1016&t=3&v0=Блантер,+Ярослав+Михайлович&f=1003&t=1&v1=&f=4&t=2&v2=&f=21&t=3&v3=&f=1016&t=3&v4=&f=1016&t=3&v5=&useExternal=true&bf=4&b=&d=0&ys=&ye=&lng=&ft=&mt=&dt=&vol=&pt=&iss=&ps=&pe=&tr=&tro=&cc=a1&i=1&v=tagged&s=0&ss=1003&st=0&i18n=ru&rlf=&psz=20&bs=20&ce=4&debug=false Search results at the Russian State Library catalogue]; [http://www.peeep.us/8a95f527 Page snapshot] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150924140903/http://www.peeep.us/8a95f527 |date=24 September 2015 }}</ref>

From 1990 to 1994, he taught [[statistical physics]], the theory of normal and superconducting metals, [[classical mechanics|classical]] and [[quantum mechanics]]. From 1989 to 1993, he also taught mathematics at the 43rd School of Moscow.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.1543.ru/teachers/remember/teachers/_full_list.htm|title=Прежние учителя 43 Школы и Гимназии 1543|trans-title=|publisher=43rd School of Moscow|language=ru-RU|access-date=17 July 2018}}</ref>

In 1995, supported by the [[Alexander von Humboldt Foundation]], he obtained a position at the Institute of Condensed Matter Theory in [[Karlsruhe]]. From 1996 to 2000, he held a position at the [[University of Geneva]]. From 2000 to 2007, he was an associate professor at the [[Delft University of Technology]]. In 2007, he became a senior associate professor there.<ref name=CV>[http://www.tnw.tudelft.nl/en/about-faculty/departments/quantum-nanoscience/peopleresearch/research-groups/theoretical-physics/people/faculty/ym-blanter/cv/ CV]. {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130320055039/http://www.tnw.tudelft.nl/en/about-faculty/departments/quantum-nanoscience/peopleresearch/research-groups/theoretical-physics/people/faculty/ym-blanter/cv/ |date=20 March 2013 }}.</ref> In 2002, he was one of three members of the organizing committee of the [[NATO]] Advanced Research Workshop "Quantum Noise in Mesoscopic Physics", held in [[Delft]], the Netherlands.<ref>{{cite book | url=https://books.google.com/books?id=YHHoCAAAQBAJ | title=Quantum Noise in Mesoscopic Physics | publisher=[[Springer Science & Business Media]] | author=Nazarov, Yuli V. | year=2012 | pages=vii| isbn=9789401000895 | via=[[Google Books]] }}</ref>

From 2007 to 2011, he was an active contributor with administrator permissions in the [[Russian Wikipedia]] and a member of its [[Arbitration Committee (Wikipedia)|Arbitration Committee]].<ref name="esq">[http://kalanbook.narod.ru/esquire_2010_1_wp.djvu Идут на поправку]. — ''[[Esquire (magazine)|Esquire]]'' (Russian edition), № 51, 2010 Jan.</ref> ''[[The Daily Dot]]'' noted Blanter's role in the deletion of an English [[Reliability of Wikipedia|Wikipedia hoax]] about a ficticous Russian filmmaker which was up for almost four years.<ref name="Daily Dot: Yuri Gadyukin"/>

==Selected works== 
Blanter has published over 100 works in several scientific journals. According to Scopus his h-factor is 47.<ref>{{Scopus id|id=7003600784}}</ref>
